raw_response:
I farm on only 7.5 mu, so I have to keep the plan tight and practical. I will keep the cabbage-chili rotation as the backbone because that fits my land, my well irrigation, and what I already know how to manage. I will put 2.5 mu into spring cabbage first and then follow that same 2.5 mu with summer chili. On the rest of the land, I will spread risk with eggplant, kidneybean, and maize, because vegetables bring cash but maize and bean help me avoid putting everything into one market. I have farmed 35 years, so I will not chase fancy changes. I will use hybrid seed for the cash vegetables and maize because I care about stable yield, and I will keep fertilizer and water a bit heavier on cabbage, chili, and eggplant since they respond well and I have well irrigation. Kidneybean needs less nitrogen, so I will keep that lighter. I will use plough tillage before the main crops because I still trust a clean, deep seedbed more than no-tillage on my small plots. I will spray only as much as needed to hold disease and insects down, especially on the vegetables, because those are the crops where damage costs me money fastest.
